market_scope: US-listed semiconductor and AI data center infrastructure stocks only

china_a_shares.reason: Excluded because filing comparability and source confidence are below the US-market screen threshold.

safe_harbor: Educational information only. Not financial advice. Prices can move materially around earnings.

quote_source.name: Official company releases, Reuters, Yahoo Finance, and public market snapshots
quote_source.note: August 27 regular closes are used where available. Marvell uses an August 28 pre-market reference after its earnings release. Approximate prices are labeled.

market_emotion.basis: NVIDIA de-risked near-term AI demand and lifted the semiconductor complex on August 27. The score remains elevated because NVIDIA already gapped 8.7%, Broadcom reports September 2, Marvell fell despite a beat and raise, and memory plus connectivity positioning remains crowded.

strict_scoring.score_formula: forward fundamental surprise + narrative and expectation shift + supply-chain moat and diffusion + valuation and reaction gap + financial quality and positioning risk + evidence integrity
strict_scoring.interpretation: The score is an ordinal research rank, not a calibrated probability, target return, or backtested alpha estimate.
hard_gates: fresh attributable filing or company evidence
no unresolved accounting or liquidity red flag
valuation and market reaction assessed against expectations
buy list may be empty when no candidate reaches 82

position_sizing_overlay.rule: Use the conviction rank only for selection. Size is reduced independently for volatility, portfolio correlation, crowding, customer concentration, liquidity, and imminent earnings risk.
position_sizing_overlay.initial_size: No more than about one-quarter of intended exposure for current staged buys, and only on an orderly pullback or support retest.
position_sizing_overlay.exit_rule: Review or exit when the guidance, demand, margin, cash-flow, or supply-chain thesis breaks; do not rely on price stops alone.

NVDA.reason: Revenue exceeded consensus by about 8.7%, EPS beat, Q3 guidance exceeded the prior estimate, GAAP gross margin was 75%, and Rubin plus memory commitments extend the runway. The 8.7% price gap prevents chase entries.

KLAC.reason: Process-control intensity, double-digit growth, strong free cash flow, and only a 0.2% August 27 move versus a roughly 1.6% SOXX gain create the cleaner underreaction setup.

AVGO.reason: AI semiconductor and networking fundamentals are excellent, but the stock gained 4.5% in sympathy and September 2 earnings are the required fresh evidence.

LRCX.reason: Revenue and earnings growth are excellent, but the rerating offers less entry margin than KLAC.

AMAT.reason: Fiscal Q3 growth and DRAM exposure are strong, but price and expectations remain elevated after the AI equipment rerating.

FORM.reason: HBM and CPO test intensity drove a major earnings inflection, but the stock has more than doubled year to date.

MU.reason: HBM and memory earnings are extraordinary and NVIDIA procurement confirms scarcity, but the price cycle and positioning remain extreme.

MRVL.reason: Revenue, data-center growth, cash flow, and guidance passed, but the negative reaction indicates Google-program timing and a roughly 58x forward multiple did not clear expectations.

PDFS.reason: Q2 passed the profit and cash-flow gate, but valuation and integration risk prevent a current best-buy rating.

CRDO.reason: AEC and connectivity exposure are attractive, but momentum, expectations, valuation, and concentration are demanding.

rankings.positioning: Quarter-size starter positions only on pullbacks or support retests; do not chase NVIDIA's post-earnings gap.

supply_chain_view.framework: Silicon to system to powered site
next_two_year_bottlenecks: HBM and DRAM allocation plus HBM4e qualification
CoWoS and advanced packaging capacity, yield, and inspection
800G and 1.6T networking, AECs, CPO, and silicon photonics
high-voltage rack power, grid interconnects, transformers, liquid cooling, and powered land
supply_chain_view.trend: Vera Rubin is in full production and NVIDIA's $279B commitment base identifies memory as the first-order constraint. Custom ASICs expand alongside merchant GPUs, while useful cluster output increasingly depends on packaging, networking, storage, power, cooling, and construction timing.

NVDA.next_guide: Q3 revenue $108B +/- 2%; GAAP gross margin about 74%; no China data-center compute revenue assumed
NVDA.supply_signal: Vera Rubin in full production; purchase and capacity commitments increased to $279B, primarily memory

MRVL.next_guide: Q3 revenue $3.15B +/- 5%; non-GAAP EPS $1.10 +/- $0.05; non-GAAP gross margin 57.5%-58.5%
MRVL.market_check: About -8% pre-market as Google custom-silicon timing and valuation disappointed elevated expectations

AVGO.status: Quality passes; fresh position is capped until September 2 earnings.

KLAC.period: FY2026 Q4 and FY2026 10-K filed August 6

MU.status: Fundamentals pass; price-cycle discipline fails today's buy gate.

source_intelligence.signal: Marvell's 37% growth and higher guide were overshadowed by valuation and custom-silicon timing.
Photonics, HBM, equipment capacity, and power plus water constraints remain foreground system dependencies.
Accelerator economics link HBM, wafer starts, packaging yields, networking, power, financing, and deployment capacity.
AI connectivity and custom-silicon theses remain constructive, but valuation grades and the actual market reaction require selectivity.
Order activity improved; generative AI, CoWoS constraints, foundry momentum, and subcontractor gains remain supportive.
Rubin-class rack demand, liquid cooling, and high-voltage DC power are becoming key 2026-2028 system constraints.
Training compute is scaling faster than power and data movement; 300mm memory equipment spending is expected above $50B, up 29%.
Rubin-class racks expose the physical bill of materials: liquid cooling, 800G networking, DPUs, storage, and power shelves.
NVLink Fusion, NVHBM, AWS GPU deployment, custom inference chips, and flash capacity show broad system scaling.
NVIDIA's longer runway lifted the sector, while Marvell's decline exposed timing and valuation risk despite strong results.
NVIDIA's post-earnings move drove a broad semiconductor rally, raising both demand confidence and short-term entry risk.
